item.text:
I would harden three things.

- [test/orders.js:20](C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:20) `averageItemPrice` should handle `[]` explicitly. Right now an empty order can produce an invalid numeric result. That is a correctness bug, not just polish.
- [test/orders.js:19](C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:19) The meaning of “average item price” is ambiguous. Today it divides total revenue by number of array entries, not total quantity. If one line has `qty: 10`, the result is misleading. I would either rename it to “average line total” or divide by summed quantity.
- [test/orders.js:5](C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:5), [test/orders.js:24](C:/Users/Kerim/AppData/Local/Temp/codex-eco-bench-J014pF/test/orders.js:24) Input validation is missing throughout. `null` items, missing `price`/`qty`, non-numeric values, negative quantities, or malformed `order.items` will throw or produce bad totals. For a backend utility, failing predictably with a clear error is safer than silently returning `NaN`.

If I were changing behavior, I’d also decide whether discounts should be case-insensitive and whether totals need rounding rules to avoid floating-point money issues.
